findings.issue: Task 3 (depends_on [1,2]) and Task 4 (depends_on [1]) are both wave 2 with no depends_on between them, yet both modify the SAME two files: news_bot.py and tests/test_integration.py. Task 3 edits the module-level REVIEW_BUTTONS_ENABLED flag (~L130) and the E014 send site (~L2374-2397); Task 4 adds a new function resolve_dedup_callback near send_admin_notification (~L469-530) and a new TestResolveDedupCallback class in test_integration.py. The regions are disjoint and the logic is independent (verified: Task 4 does not reference REVIEW_BUTTONS_ENABLED or the send site, Task 3 does not reference resolve_dedup_callback), so there is no logical/hidden-dependency problem -- but running two agents in true parallel against the same two files in the same wave is a mechanical merge-conflict risk that the checklist's dependency-graph view doesn't capture.
findings.fix: No spec change needed. Feature-execution should apply wave-2 tasks to news_bot.py / tests/test_integration.py sequentially (or diff-merge explicitly) even though the dependency graph marks them parallel-safe, since 'no depends_on between two tasks' here means 'independent content', not 'independent files'.
